 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Bhaskar Shankar  For the Respondent/s : Mr.Arvind Kumar Pandey (App  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE BIBEK CHAUDHURI  ORAL ORDER 3 09-07-2025
This is an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay by 228 days in filing the instant revision.
The petitioner is the informant of Mahila P.S. Case No. 68/2017 registered under 498A/120B of the IPC and Sections  of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The trial court convicted the accused persons/opposite parties.
The accused persons preferred an appeal before the learned Additional Patna High Court CR. REV. No.520 of 2024(3) dt.09-07-2025 Sessions Judge-XI, Kaimur at Bhabhua.
The concerned learned Additional Sessions Judge set aside the order of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court and remanded the case back to the trial court for re-trial.
The said order is under challenge in the instant revision.
2. It is submitted by the petitioner that the petitioner did not know about the date of delivery of judgment of the appellate court.
The learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioner assured him that he would inform the petitioner about the date of final disposal of the appeal, but he did not do the same.
He came to know about the result of the appeal at a belated stage.

It is further stated by the Jai Govind Rai vs The State Of Bihar on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160247606/
1 petitioner that he did not receive any summons after the case was remanded back to the trial court.

sentences.text: He came to know from some co-villagers about the judgment passed by the appellate court.
Therefore, there was delay of 228 days in filing the revisional application.

3. Having appeared the learned Advocate for the petitioner and on careful perusal of the application,
I find that the petitioner has been able to make out a sufficient ground for condonation of delay,
therefore, the application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act is allowed.
4.
The instant criminal revision is admitted.

Patna High Court CR. REV. No.520 of 2024(3)
dt.09-07-2025 5.

Issue notice to the private opposite parties no. 2 to 7 by both modes, i.e., under ordinary process as well as registered cover with A/D, on steps being taken by the petitioner for filing requisites etc.,
within a period of one week from the date of this order.

6. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the period of delay in filing the limitation petition was earlier mentioned as 69 days when it ought to have been 228 days in the I.A. No.1 of 2024.
As such, learned counsel for the petitioner prays for making necessary correction in the same.
7. Permission is accorded.
8. The instant revision shall be listed under the heading "For Admission" after the receipt of service of notice.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J) Suraj Dubey/-
